question: Serum uric acid may be within the normal reference range during an acute gout attack, so a normal result does not exclude the diagnosis of gout.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE and is an important clinical trap. Serum uric acid falls during the acute inflammatory phase of gout; a 'normal' result during the attack does NOT rule out gout. Synovial fluid crystal analysis (negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals) is the definitive test.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. During acute gout, the inflammatory response triggers a transient uricosuric effect that lowers serum uric acid — sometimes to within the normal range. Serum uric acid is most reliably measured 2–4 weeks after the acute attack has resolved.
